text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New government under Dr Majali. King Hussein sets out government priorities in letter of appointment. Says focus on domestic issues and rooting out negative factors.
- Majali says will work to strengthen democracy, build civil society and support justice. Elections to be held on time and obstacles to investment will be removed.
- King to head to United States on Friday for health check. Meeting with Clinton to be fixed next week.
- Majali's cabinet to hold their first meeting today.
- Majali forms a government to ensure the coming stage.
- 24-member cabinet includes five from previous cabinet and 13 who have not held ministerial posts before.
- King Hussein appoints Majali government to clear up administration and oversee clean elections.
- Two mini-governments within the cabinet focusing on domestic issues. One headed by Abdullah Ensour, tackling administrative reform, another headed by Jawad al-Anani, tackling economic development.
- Majali's 23-member government is sworn in. Four members of Kabariti government retained; most newcomers are technocrats with long experience.
- New premier says merits, not influence, should guide civil service appointments.
- New cabinet seen to have potential for change but faces challenges.
- King Hussein receives Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat.
